one_line: Turns browser failures into verified recovery evidence and reusable regression tests.
what_it_does: A structured WebMCP QA control plane captures a stale-selector failure, verifies a safe fallback, retries it, and exports a Playwright test.
leverage_rationale: Typed, stateful failure inspection and guarded recovery are materially more reliable than an agent guessing through a browser UI; the shared evidence and verified selector are central to the workflow.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies six narrow tools for test creation, runs, failure inspection, guarded retry, and export.
Frame sheet shows a coherent test interface progressing to a visible failure/error state and evidence area.
execution_rationale: The stated central workflow is coherent and the video visibly shows a real testing interface, controls, and failure output, though the final exported test is not legible in the frames.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows browser-test setup, run controls, distinct result/evidence regions, and a reproduced red failure state.
Description states the demo reaches Order confirmed and exports a Playwright TypeScript regression test.
impact_rationale: Browser-test brittleness is a concrete problem for developers and QA teams, and evidence-backed recovery can reduce unsafe or opaque automation failures.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly targets brittle browser failures and reusable regression coverage.
Description identifies stale selectors, evidence capture, DOM inspection, and safe fallback recovery.
creativity_rationale: The combination of WebMCP shared state, evidence preservation, and proof-gated recovery is a fresh and memorable treatment of browser automation QA.
creativity_evidence: Product frames and pitch center on converting a failure into a verified regression artifact rather than silently guessing.
usability_note: The staged control-plane flow appears understandable, though technical QA concepts may be unfamiliar to casual users.
red_flags: The final exported test is not clearly legible in the frame sheet.
standouts: Proof-gated selector recovery with preserved browser evidence.
advance_reason: Strong differentiated WebMCP use case with credible product evidence.

one_line: Lets browser agents compile, flash, and inspect USB-connected microcontrollers.
what_it_does: Chip bridges a browser dashboard, Web Serial, backend build jobs, and live ESP32 status so an agent can participate in the hardware loop.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP gives the agent scoped access to the live browser session and USB-connected board, which a general UI-driving agent cannot comparably achieve reliably.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly says WebMCP connects the agent to the live browser session holding Web Serial access.
Listed tools include device enumeration, board status, serial logs, job status, user action requests, and erase.
execution_rationale: The frames show a functioning technical dashboard with configuration/output and a selection dialog, but the exact flash success and hardware response are not clearly readable.
execution_evidence: Frame sheet shows consistent dashboard/sidebar, configuration fields, technical output/log panel, state changes, and a modal selection flow.
Description specifies compile, flash, status, serial monitoring, and safety-oriented user actions.
impact_rationale: Hardware beginners and makers face substantial friction across toolchains, drivers, flashing, and serial debugging; collapsing that loop has credible value.
impact_evidence: Pitch identifies the gap between AI-generated firmware and the physical ESP32.
Description targets compile/flash/debug workflow and browser-based USB access.
creativity_rationale: Direct agent interaction with physical microcontrollers through browser-native Web Serial is an unusually ambitious and memorable WebMCP application.
creativity_evidence: The concept connects browser agents to live physical hardware rather than only manipulating web data.
usability_note: The dashboard could simplify a difficult workflow, but hardware permissions and setup remain nontrivial.
red_flags: Video frames do not clearly prove a successful physical flash or serial result.
standouts: Browser-to-ESP32 agent bridge via Web Serial.
advance_reason: Exceptional leverage and ambition despite incomplete visible end-state evidence.

one_line: A persistent, inspectable personal OS for goals, reflection, and evidence-grounded advice.
what_it_does: Consilium stores longitudinal goals and journal context, generates explainable priorities and reflections, and lets a browser agent act within visible user-controlled state.
leverage_rationale: Persistent structured history, citations, confidence, and visible state effects give the agent a substantially better context and control surface than ordinary browser driving.
leverage_evidence: Description details structured goals, longitudinal evidence, advisor sources, and transparent WebMCP calls.
Frames show journal/evening reflection, recorded context, and conversion into operational memory.
execution_rationale: The frames show multiple coherent screens and a complete-looking reflection-to-memory flow, but do not prove persistence or successful agent mutations.
execution_evidence: Frames visibly progress from overview to Journal & Evening Reflection, operational memory, and structured reflection prompts.
Description names goals, projects, morning brief, advisors, analytics, and user control.
impact_rationale: People managing complex personal goals can benefit from durable context and evidence-grounded reflection; the niche audience and personal value are credible.
impact_evidence: Product presents a specific use case around goals, history, decisions, and daily reflection.
Frames show concrete structured prompts and fictional Maya context rather than only a landing page.
creativity_rationale: The personal-OS framing, council of source-bounded advisors, and operational-memory conversion are a fresh synthesis beyond a generic task planner.
creativity_evidence: Frames show the unusual transition from lived journal context to operational memory.
Description emphasizes disagreement, citations, and non-autonomous companionship.
usability_note: The staged reflection workflow is clear but potentially demanding for daily use.
red_flags: Submission says the system predates the challenge; end-to-end agent invocation is not visible.
standouts: Evidence-backed personal memory and reflection without surrendering control.
advance_reason: Strong concept and visible product flow, with some uncertainty around observed agent execution.

one_line: An agent-native EHR assistant that works inside the doctor’s active session.
what_it_does: Doctors use chat or voice to inspect patient status, navigate notes, and prepare/sign consultations while permissions and final approval remain in-session.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP uniquely keeps the agent inside the already-authorized EHR tab and exposes only context-scoped actions; removing it makes the proposed integration effectively unshippable.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly argues external API/OAuth integration is blocked by hospital credential and security constraints.
Frames show natural-language instructions leading into patient records, Notes, and a patient detail view.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates navigation from an assistant prompt into a populated patient-record UI and notes workflow, but does not clearly show the note saved or signed.
execution_evidence: Frames show patient list, patient profile labeled ER, Notes-related controls, and narrated step progression.
Description states doctor-controlled patient status checks and consultation signing.
impact_rationale: Clinicians have a clear time and attention problem in documentation-heavy visits, and an in-session assistant could return time to patient care while preserving physician sign-off.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets what 15-minute visits miss and physician documentation burden.
Description identifies concrete EHR tasks and human approval boundary.
creativity_rationale: The shared-tab, permission-scoped EHR agent model is an ambitious and compelling application of WebMCP to a high-stakes workflow.
creativity_evidence: Frames visibly connect conversational instruction with a medical-record interface.
Description frames WebMCP as the enabling security and authorization model.
usability_note: Conversational control could reduce clicks, but clinical safety and review requirements make the workflow necessarily careful.
red_flags: The final generated note/save/sign state is not clearly shown; medical claims require strict validation.
standouts: In-session EHR control without handing credentials to a second-party integration.
advance_reason: High impact and transformative leverage with visible agent-to-EHR workflow.

one_line: A fictional marketplace that exposes and removes paid influence from agent recommendations.
what_it_does: It captures a bounded intent, simulates advertiser influence, shows an influence receipt, applies a user policy, and compares the sponsored ranking with a clean room.
leverage_rationale: Structured intent, auction, policy, receipt, and clean-room tools make recommendation influence inspectable and repeatable in shared state; generic UI automation would be less precise.
leverage_evidence: Description enumerates seven page-defined tools across intent, auction, receipt, policy, comparison, and staging.
Frames show bounded brief, decision review, synthetic bidstream, simulated auction, and human removal stages.
execution_rationale: The fixed scenario and storyboard visibly communicate a coherent multi-step experiment with decision review and deterministic outcome, though the auction is synthetic by design.
execution_evidence: Frames show consistent decision-review UI and explicit staged captions for intent, auction, bidstream, and removal.
Description gives concrete OmniMotion/KinoForge scores and a no-purchase boundary.
impact_rationale: As agents mediate purchasing and research, transparent disclosure of paid influence is a credible public-interest and consumer-protection use case.
impact_evidence: Pitch directly addresses hidden commercial influence in agent recommendations.
Product compares sponsored and sponsor-free results and exposes contribution points.
creativity_rationale: The concept is unusually original, socially pointed, and deeply pursued through receipts, counterfactual clean-room comparison, and live human policy intervention.
creativity_evidence: Frames and description show the memorable market-versus-clean-room interaction model.
Fixed fixture makes the manipulation measurable rather than merely rhetorical.
usability_note: The staged review and receipt model appears legible, though the fictional auction is conceptually dense.
red_flags: The marketplace and auction are explicitly fictional/synthetic, limiting claims about real-world efficacy.
standouts: A concrete, inspectable counterfactual for paid recommendation influence.
advance_reason: Highly original concept with strong visible workflow and evidence model.

one_line: A no-code Framer plugin that publishes typed WebMCP tools for sites.
what_it_does: AgentReady scans Framer projects, lets creators choose capabilities, and generates a secure runtime exposing tools for content, forms, commerce, payments, and workflows.
leverage_rationale: The product’s core value is creating an agent-native surface that ordinary browser automation cannot provide with comparable typed semantics, permissions, and discoverability.
leverage_evidence: Description says the plugin publishes a top-level runtime and up to 30 typed tools.
Frames visibly show branded tool categories, configuration panels, toggles, and a site-tool setup flow.
execution_rationale: The visual evidence shows a substantial, coherent configuration product with many capability categories and progressive setup, though live end-user invocation is not shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show sidebar navigation, tool selection, configuration forms, toggles, previews, and publish-style controls.
Description lists concrete Framer scanning and runtime-generation behavior.
impact_rationale: Framer creators are a clear audience, and no-code publication of agent capabilities could materially expand the number of sites usable by agents.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets any Framer site and explicitly removes code/schema/security integration work.
Description covers forms, CMS, commerce, payments, content, and AI workflows.
creativity_rationale: A no-code WebMCP builder embedded in a visual site-builder is a strong and ambitious productization of the protocol.
creativity_evidence: The concept spans many site surfaces while preserving creator-selected capabilities.
Frames show an actual admin/configuration experience rather than only an API claim.
usability_note: The no-code configuration model is promising, though thirty tools and advanced options could overwhelm creators.
red_flags: Video shows configuration and publishing surfaces more clearly than a completed live agent transaction.
standouts: Protocol adoption packaged for nontechnical Framer creators.
advance_reason: High leverage and audience fit with substantial visible implementation evidence.

one_line: Turns a repair photo and symptom into a shared, constrained repair workbench.
what_it_does: OpenRepair maintains evidence, hypotheses, component context, questions, constraints, safety checks, and a human-approved repair plan while an agent edits the live inspection.
leverage_rationale: The agent contributes to a shared, versioned evidence artifact with stale-write rejection, constraint checks, and safety boundaries; this is more than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies eight WebMCP tools and shared live state.
Frames show a bicycle illustration, changing highlighted region, structured review panel, action control, and feedback toasts.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence visibly demonstrates an interactive image/review task with annotation changes, structured controls, and system feedback; the full repair recommendation is not legible.
execution_evidence: Frames show persistent bicycle task context and refined orange component annotation across states.
Visible checklist/form panel, submit-style control, and repeated toast feedback indicate an active workflow.
impact_rationale: DIY repairers and technicians have a real need for diagnosis under uncertainty, parts constraints, and safety limits; preserving human approval makes the value credible.
impact_evidence: Description gives a concrete bicycle chain-skipping scenario with budget and cassette-preservation constraints.
Product separates evidence, hypotheses, repair paths, and final approval.
creativity_rationale: The evolving inspection artifact and agent-human collaboration model are an original, thoughtful alternative to one-shot generic repair tutorials.
creativity_evidence: Frames visibly combine visual component annotation with structured review state.
Description emphasizes correction-driven reranking, reversibility, and safety stops.
usability_note: A guided evidence workbench can make uncertain repair decisions clearer, though the amount of structured review may be substantial.
red_flags: Frame text is small and does not clearly show the final validated repair plan.
standouts: Constraint-aware diagnosis with visible human approval and reversible actions.
advance_reason: Strong shared-state concept with credible visual interaction evidence.

one_line: A local-first context-pack control plane for personal agents.
what_it_does: Compass stores notes, tasks, bookmarks, and snippets, then exposes a permission- and pack-scoped WebMCP surface with live audit and undo.
leverage_rationale: The first-class Context Pack creates a visible, revocable boundary for what an agent can read or write, with registry changes and handler checks tied to that state.
leverage_evidence: Description details ten typed tools, active-pack scoping, live read/write switches, audit entries, and Undo.
Frames show Compass control-plane branding, a visible Context Pack, structured data, count summary, and activation control.
execution_rationale: The video visibly presents a coherent context-pack dashboard and connected-tool model; persistence and undo are described but not directly proven by the frames.
execution_evidence: Frames show hub-and-spoke Compass overview and a structured One visible Context Pack workflow.
Description specifies IndexedDB persistence, validation, shared permissions, audit, and a fictional Atlas demo flow.
impact_rationale: People want useful personal agents without exposing an entire workspace; explicit context and write boundaries address a concrete privacy/control problem.
impact_evidence: Pitch centers on personal context, rules, and agent control.
Description gives practical notes/tasks/bookmarks use cases and a safe enable-disable-undo flow.
creativity_rationale: Making the context boundary itself a manipulable, temporary product object is a strong interaction innovation for personal agents.
creativity_evidence: Frames explicitly center a visible Context Pack rather than an opaque authorization screen.
Description combines local-first storage, scoped tools, immediate registry rebuilding, and auditability.
usability_note: The visible-pack metaphor and live permission controls support comprehension, though the control plane has significant conceptual surface area.
red_flags: The frames show the context-pack setup more clearly than the agent write/undo sequence.
standouts: Revocable context packs make agent authorization tangible and inspectable.
advance_reason: Clear audience problem, strong leverage, and substantial visible product flow.

one_line: Turns benchmark outputs into interactive, human-and-agent acceptance checks.
what_it_does: Arena filters published checks, has an agent play shortlisted anonymous games through WebMCP, and turns human taste plus fixed evidence into a future test harness.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP lets an agent inspect benchmark evidence and exercise playable outputs in the same page, extending static scores into repeatable live evaluation.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies 22 checks reduced to seven, four games completed through WebMCP, and a generated harness plan.
Frames show comparison cards, a benchmark chart, detailed results table, and persistent build prompt/workspace.
execution_rationale: The frame sequence visibly covers build prompt, comparison gallery, benchmark visualization, and detailed table, coherently matching the described evaluation loop; actual gameplay completion is not visually obvious.
execution_evidence: Frames show headline Compare coding agents by feel, output cards, scatter-style benchmark chart, and tabular results.
Description provides a concrete recorded flow from published checks to anonymous shortlist and harness plan.
impact_rationale: Developers selecting agents need both measurable checks and subjective fit; this addresses a genuine gap in benchmark-only evaluation.
impact_evidence: Pitch explicitly distinguishes fixed benchmark scores from workflow-specific failure modes and feel.
Product preserves scores while adding live verification and human choice.
creativity_rationale: Using playable outputs as evaluation evidence and combining agent testing with anonymous human taste is a notably original interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Frames visibly combine generated UI cards, quantitative plots, and detailed benchmark data.
Description turns subjective comparison into concrete future acceptance checks.
usability_note: The gallery-to-benchmark flow is legible, though evaluation concepts and anonymous comparisons may require orientation.
red_flags: Frames do not clearly show the agent completing the four playable scenarios.
standouts: Benchmarks become living, workflow-specific acceptance checks rather than a frozen leaderboard.
advance_reason: Distinctive evaluation concept with credible visible product surfaces.

one_line: An evidence-first workspace for safely reviewing suspicious job offers.
what_it_does: Offroof extracts exact offer excerpts into deterministic signals, separates observation from inference, and builds a consented reversible verification checklist.
leverage_rationale: Semantic tools operate on the same visible, versioned case while separating reads, analysis, and consented mutations; structured evidence is materially safer than an agent clicking through a page.
leverage_evidence: Description specifies six tools for case summary, signal inspection, plan building, guarded updates, official resources, and receipts.
Frames show offer review, a payment-request signal, source excerpt linkage, and an Observed evidence and verification record screen.
execution_rationale: The video visibly demonstrates a coherent offer-to-evidence workflow with source excerpts, verification steps, and structured records, though the final checklist mutation is not fully shown.
execution_evidence: Frames show suspicious offer language, highlighted warning, extracted payment-request signal, and evidence record.
Description specifies privacy-cleaned import, exact excerpt attachment, consent, version guards, and receipts.
impact_rationale: Job seekers face real financial and social-engineering risk, and a calm tool that avoids unsupported fraud labels while guiding verification has clear value.
impact_evidence: Pitch targets suspicious job offers and evidence before action.
Description explicitly avoids opening links, sending money, or declaring safe/fraudulent and provides official Korean resources.
creativity_rationale: The careful separation of literal text, bounded inference, unknowns, and next verification steps is a thoughtful and differentiated safety interaction.
creativity_evidence: Frames show source-backed signals and an evidence/verification record rather than a binary verdict.
Description makes privacy, reversibility, and human control core product mechanics.
usability_note: The calm, excerpt-linked workflow and explicit next steps appear well suited to users under pressure.
red_flags: The frame sheet does not clearly show a live agent tool-call panel.
standouts: Evidence/inference separation avoids overclaiming while still producing actionable verification.
advance_reason: High practical impact and strong evidence-centered execution.
